slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: At slightly acid pH, albumin changes the colour of the bromocresol green indicator from yellow-green to green-blue.
The colour intensity is proportional to the albumin concentration in the sample.
Albumin is made in the liver; changes are seen in liver disease, malnutrition, skin lesions (dermatitis, burns) or dehydration.

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Albumin” kit (IFU BSIS02-I, 11/02/16). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or plasma free of haemolysis — stable for 1 month at 2–8 °C or 1 week at 15–25 °C.
Reagent: bromocresol green pH 4.2, 0.12 mmol/L. Standard: albumin 5 g/dL (aqueous primary standard).
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 630 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The reagent and standard are ready to use.
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light until expiry.
Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 630 nm ≥ 0.40.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
The values come from the SPINREACT “Albumin” IFU (BSIS02-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 630 nm (600–650); temperature 15–25 °C or 37 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — reagent 1.0 mL; standard — reagent 1.0 mL + standard 5 µL; sample — reagent 1.0 mL + sample 5 µL.
4. Mix and incubate: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at 15–25 °C.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank; the colour is stable for 1 hour at room temperature.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: albumin programme
rows: Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (g/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 5 (standard concentration).
Conversion: g/dL × 144.9 = µmol/L.
Linear up to 6 g/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.
IFU reference: 3.5–5.0 g/dL.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Bilirubin up to 110 mg/L, haemoglobin up to 1 g/L and lipaemia up to 10 g/L do not interfere.
The sample must be free of haemolysis (IFU requirement).
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
